item.text: I’m validating the strongest 2024 macro and governance signals for this lens: inflation handling, sanctions/war effects, and whether the Kremlin told a straight story or blamed outsiders. Then I’ll stop searching and synthesize only the claims that matter.

item.text:
**5B.9, 2024: mixed at best, mostly no**
Putin showed some narrow crisis-management competence in late 2024, especially by deferring to tight central-bank policy. But the broader pattern was war-distorted growth, tax extraction, opacity, and blame-shifting rather than consistently competent and honest management of shocks.

| Stance | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Support | Russian central bank keeps rates on hold after Putin's call for 'balance' | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-12-20 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-central-bank-keeps-rates-on-hold-after-putins-call-for-balance-3784135 | Putin publicly backed the central bank’s tight policy instead of overriding it, and the bank said earlier tightening was creating conditions for disinflation. This is the clearest sign of some competence and deference to expertise. | 5B.9, 5B.6 |
| Support | Putin says Russia's economy is overheating, inflation is worrying | Reuters via MarketScreener | 2024-12-19 | https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Putin-says-Russia-s-economy-is-overheating-inflation-is-worrying-48625233/ | Putin acknowledged overheating and high inflation and said the government and central bank needed to slow the economy. That is real admission of a macro problem, though it was paired with blame-shifting. | 5B.9, 5B.7 |
| Support | Russian economy shows solid growth despite Ukraine war sanctions | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756 | Russia sustained headline growth and record-low unemployment despite sanctions, showing short-run resilience and crisis containment. The same report makes clear that much of the growth came from military production. | 5B.9, 5B.6 |
| Against | Analysis-Russia braces for more tax rises to fund the Ukraine war | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-10-31 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/analysisrussia-braces-for-more-tax-rises-to-fund-the-ukraine-war-3693480 | Economists said Russia would need more tax rises to finance ballooning military spending. That points to extraction and war financing rather than competent stabilization of the broader economy. | 5B.9, 5B.6 |
| Against | Putin lets 'economically significant' entities limit information disclosures | Reuters | 2024-01-29 | https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001 | Widening secrecy for major firms reduced scrutiny and made it harder to judge economic conditions honestly. That weakens transparent crisis management. | 5B.9, 5B.4, 5B.5 |
| Against | Analysis: Russia's GDP boost on military spending belies wider economic woes | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-02-07 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/analysisrussias-gdp-boost-on-military-spending-belies-wider-economic-woes-3295688 | Reuters said the growth rebound rested heavily on state arms production and masked broader civilian weakness. That is evidence of war-driven distortion, not clean or honest economic management. | 5B.9, 5B.6 |
| Against | Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says corruption is pervasive, elites get contracts and protection for loyalty, and decision-making is opaque. That is strong background evidence against honest, accountable crisis management. | 5B.9, 5B.5, 5B.7 |
| Against | Putin says Russia's economy is overheating, inflation is worrying | Reuters via MarketScreener | 2024-12-19 | https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Putin-says-Russia-s-economy-is-overheating-inflation-is-worrying-48625233/ | In the same remarks, Putin blamed Western sanctions and a bad harvest for high prices. That is partial acknowledgment combined with scapegoating rather than full honesty. | 5B.9, 5B.7 |

Search gap: I found no strong 2024 example of Putin clearly learning from a shock, openly admitting policy error, and reversing course on that basis. The best pro evidence is limited to late-year monetary restraint and acknowledging inflation; the stronger evidence shows war-driven distortion, opacity, and blame-shifting.
